newsitem.title: PERU: Southern Peru's Jan-Oct output up 26.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Southern Peru's Jan-Oct output up 26.8 percent.

text.p: Copper mine output at Southern Peru Ltd reached 258,268 tonnes in the first ten months of the year, up 26.75 percent compared with the same period last year, the government said Monday.

Majority owned by ASARCO Inc and Peru's largest copper producer, Southern accounted for 64.5 percent of Peru's total output in the first ten months, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry's preliminary figures.
These figures were for copper produced at Southern's Cuajone and Toquepala open-pit mines.
Peru's copper production rose 17 percent to 54,422 tonnes in the first ten months of the year compared with the same period last year.
The country's higher output was due mainly to increased production at Southern, Cyprus Amax Minerals Co's Cerro Verde open pit annd at state-owned mining giant Centromin Peru S.A..

Output in the first ten months at Cyprus's Sociedad Minera Cerro Verde S.A., Peru's third largest copper miner, rose to 35,590 tonnes, up 49.52 percent compared with the same period last year. Cerro Verde was privatized in December 1993.
At Centromin, the fourth largest producer, production jumped to 31,919 tonnes in the first ten months, up 11.71 percent.

Meanwhile, ten-month output at the country's second largest producer, Magma Copper Co's Tintaya mine, fell 14.51 percent to 47,020 tonnes. The former state-run Tintaya mine was sold to U.S.-based Magma in November 1994.
Copper is Peru's largest single export earner, accounting for $1.199 billion or 21.5 percent of total Peruvian exports in 1995, according to official figures.
The world's sixth largest copper producer, Peru saw output of the red metal climb 10.8 percent to 404,990 tonnes last year compared with 365,513 tonnes the previous year.
